name: review-gate
description: The review gate as a tool.check function hook. Every shell call is decided in process, so the non-commit calls -- almost all of them -- cost no subprocess at all, and a blocked commit can be put to you as a question instead of refused outright. The decision itself is still bin/review-gate, run only for a command that mentions a commit, so both routes read the same receipts and cannot disagree.

blocked.title: What a blocked commit does
blocked.description: "ask" (default) puts the gate's reason to you as a permission prompt, which the shell-hook route cannot do: it can only refuse and hand the agent a reason. "deny" refuses the commit outright, matching REVIEW_GATE=block exactly.

gate.title: Path to the review-gate script
gate.description: Where bin/review-gate lives. Left unset, the hook looks at AI_REVIEW_GATE_BIN, then ~/.local/bin/review-gate, then review-gate on PATH, and stays out of the way entirely if it finds none.
